newsitem.title: INDIA: India police start detentions ahead of Miss World.
newsitem.headline: India police start detentions ahead of Miss World.

text.p: Bangalore police said on Friday they will begin detaining militant activists ahead of Saturday's controversial Miss World beauty pageant, which has provoked threats of multiple suicide protests.

Members of a traditionalist women's group, the Mahila Jagran Samiti, led by a law student Kinay Narayana Shashikala has threatened to burn themselves alive unless the show in the southern Indian city is stopped.
"Preventive arrests will start. We're keeping a close watch on the lady Shashikala," police commissioner S.C. Burman told Reuters. "But we have not yet decided to detain her."
Burman said he was concerned about potential trouble spoiling the three-hour extravaganza, which will be watched by a television audience estimated at two billion in 115 countries.
"I'm apprehensive but that does not mean we're going to run away. I believe in looking the tiger in the eye," he said.

He had no comment on a threat by a group calling themselves the Indian Tigers that 400 activists would infiltrate the crowds around Saturday night's show and carry out lightning attacks inside and outside the stadium.
"We are prepared for every eventuality," he said.
